What exactly is happening inside the Tata Group after the passing of Ratan Tata Sir? Is the massive Rs 45 Lakh Crore empire actually in danger, or is there a hidden boardroom power struggle being kept from the public? In this video, we aren't just talking in the air—we are diving deep into the hard data, the internal battles, and the shocking crash of Tata Motors in 2026.

The Boardroom War: Noel Tata vs SP Group
A massive cold war has started between Tata Trusts and the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group. The stability that existed during Ratan Tata's era has been shaken. With Noel Tata stepping in, the heavy internal politics over board appointments and ultimate control has put a massive question mark on the future of Tata Sons. In this video, we decode who the real masterminds are and whether this internal politics is actually destroying the Tata legacy from the inside.

Why Tata Motors is Crashing (The Financial Breakdown)
If everything is fine within the group, why did Tata Motors shares crash to a 52-week low? A massive 29% drop in recent times is not a small issue. What is the real truth behind the commercial vehicle (CV) and passenger vehicle (PV) demerger? Why did the ₹1,643 crore in one-time exceptional costs send investors into a panic? I will break down the complete, data-backed calculation for you.

The $180 Billion IPO Battle & Global Threats
The SP Group is pushing hard for a Tata Sons IPO to unlock their value, while Tata Trusts is fighting to avoid dividing its power and control. What will be the end result of this war? On top of that, Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran has issued serious warnings regarding supply chain disruptions and geopolitical tensions in West Asia—how heavily will this impact Tata Steel and other verticals?

Tata’s overall balance sheet is still strong (with profits hitting ₹26,232 crore), but the internal fire is pushing the group into uncharted territory. Understanding this is critical for every investor and every Indian.
